title: Terminated unsigned-byte widening
summary: Recovered the free cdecl helper at VA 0x425c40 (59 bytes). It halves the unsigned byte capacity, widens source bytes without encoding conversion, reserves one 16-bit slot, and always writes a 16-bit terminator, including capacities 0 and 1. No object fields, globals, imports, allocation or FS accesses. Two direct callers at 0x4157b8 and 0x415832 pass 512-byte stack buffers and discard EAX. Original evidence and the accepted reference were checked directly against Game.exe. Readable implementation compiled with GCC and pinned MSVC O1, O2 and O2 /Oy-; no byte-matching claim.
test_description: Freestanding GCC i386 test links the accepted reference at 0x425c40. 576 separate-buffer cases span empty through 511-byte sources, all nonzero byte values, capacities 0 through small odd/even boundaries and 510..513; two additional cases cover high-bit/maximum unsigned sizes with short sources. Compare every destination word against the original and independent expectations, including prefix/suffix canaries, and verify all source bytes remain unchanged. 2448 overlapping-buffer cases compare all 128 bytes, testing source/store ordering. Accepted 59-byte reference binary compared exactly with the original PE section. test_main returned zero.
known_limits: Source-level return type is unresolved: nonempty original path leaves EAX zero, empty path leaves the destination address. Observed callers ignore EAX; recovered API models void and does not reproduce incidental register contents.

Null, inaccessible and undersized actual storage cause invalid memory access in the original; tests always supply readable source and at least two writable destination bytes, even when nominal capacity is zero.

Portable interface uses aligned uint16_t destination storage; original x86 instructions can also store at unaligned addresses. Unaligned pointers, concurrent access and fault timing are not modeled or tested.
Original bytewise widening is not Unicode decoding. Scope excludes the virtual source provider and subsequent caller formatting behavior.
